correctness.rationale: All connected spanning cactus states are determined by retaining every bridge and omitting at most one edge per cycle. The unique block-cut path gives an exact additive shortest-distance increment over omitted cycle edges, hence endpoint payoff changes are independent and equal to q_endpoint(e)-alpha on deletion or alpha-q_endpoint(e) on addition. Therefore the stated cycle potential increases on every improving move and the tie-aware equilibrium product formula follows. Summing ordered pair distances gives the welfare identity and separate cycle maximization. The triangle-plus-two-stars family is checked analytically. The supplementary exact-rational script executed 1093 instances and 26710 state checks, including exhaustive subgraph completeness for 1526 small connected states. Computation does not replace the infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: The result resolves an entire natural structural host class in a formation game shown to lack potential on unrestricted graphs: every unilateral/bilateral improvement terminates, equilibrium existence/counts are explicit for all parameters, and welfare optima and inefficiency are computable exactly. This is not a routine cycle-only example or generic finite enumeration; the cross-cycle block-additivity lemma is the structural mechanism.
